unsupported.why: Neither the input file, the brief, the trigger nor the shared memory names an RTE or says the RTE owns this gate. The role is assumed. It is a minor point because the line only says who should receive the questions.

notes:
Every factual statement in the output matches the input file (org.calendar_rules.md at commit 9690c9b) or the brief and trigger: system demo on 24 October 2026 at 15:00; PROD window 11:00-12:00 on the day after the demo, 25 October 2026; timezone Asia/Kolkata; holidays 'None in the window'. The 11:00-12:00 window also matches the workbook action. The line 'window date equals the trigger date (2026-10-25)' follows directly from record:intake. The provenance line 'input at commit 9690c9b' matches the brief and the input header comment. The input body cites a different commit, 9404ef3, and the output silently drops it. That is acceptable but worth knowing.

Completeness: two of the five items in the workbook action, iteration dates and release train dates, are missing. The agent did not invent them, said they are missing, and raised them as open items. That is the right grounded behaviour, but without these dates the outcome 'Approved calendar rules' is only partly met.

Usefulness gap: by a manual calendar count (I could not run a date command because the step hook blocks shell), 25 October 2026 is a Sunday and 24 October 2026 is a Saturday. So the source places the system demo on a Saturday and the PROD window on a Sunday. The output only asks the gate to 'Confirm ... that the PROD window falls on a working day'. It does not say the date is a Sunday, which is the most useful thing it could tell the reviewer. Also, 'None in the window' for holidays is copied from the source with no list of holidays for the release train, so holiday coverage is thin. No numbers or dates in the output lack a source.
